scope: Exploratory equal-subset-fit-budget control added after original test access; development only. One random seed is one search-variance probe, not evidence of universal superiority.

design.sampling: Four independent uniform subsets; no replacement within a subset; groups stored in canonical day order.
design.objective: Equal mean of the two full-denominator temporal validation NDCG@10 values; stable item-ID tie breaking.
design.pool: Existing V4 sampled training rows and complete common validation candidates/truths; no resampling or target injection.

shared_precompute.description: The original two all-window CatBoost parameter fits supply the shared fixed hyperparameters; their train-fitted importance supplies the importance order. Cost is common to both conditional searches, not hidden or repeated.

design.budget_interpretation: Matched subset-fit count, cardinalities, fixed parameters and 2000-tree cap; elapsed CPU time need not be identical. Shared all-window precompute cost is reported separately. No search expansion after observing random results.

fit_record.selection_adaptation: full NDCG on continuous-model tree-prefix grid

limitations: Four subsets from one preset RNG seed do not characterize random-search variance.
The same development weeks select tree counts and the best subset for both procedures.
Point estimates compare these bounded procedures; no new significance or confirmatory-test claim.
Original final test was already observed before this control; it is not a new untouched confirmation.

Random feature blocks use canonical day order; original importance blocks use importance order. For these fixed draws the orders differ only for the five-window random trial. Column serialization can affect fixed-seed CatBoost behavior, so this is a bounded procedural comparison, not a pure causal estimate of the selection rule. No fits were repeated to remove this nuisance.

comparison.interpretation: Best-of-four development point estimates under the fixed conditional search budget; not a significance claim or an untouched-test result.
